slides.headline: He operated on a patient 10,000 km away. The round trip took under 150 milliseconds.
Dr. Mohit Bhandari performed the world's longest-distance robotic telesurgery between Australia and India
slides.body: On May 2, 2026, he remotely performed a live robotic gastrojejunostomy on a patient in Indore while operating from Perth, Australia - roughly 10,000 km away - using SS Innovations' SSI Mantra telesurgery system, during the Royal Australasian College of Surgeons' Annual Scientific Congress.

slides.headline: A three-minute procedure, with latency low enough to trust a scalpel to.
slides.body: The demonstration recorded round-trip latency under 150 milliseconds - fast enough for precise surgical control across continents - and completed the procedure in about three minutes, a landmark for how close long-distance robotic telesurgery is to real clinical use.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs specialist surgery to reach patients, not just patients to reach specialists.
slides.body: Telesurgery at this latency means a surgeon's expertise can travel instantly, even when the surgeon can't - a real path toward closing India's rural-urban specialist gap.
